title: kv-cache-attn-kernel-seqlen-edgecase-debug-scratchpad
content:
Context:
This is a scratchpad for debugging a recurring flakiness observed when serving long-context requests (~>4096 tokens) where outputs sometimes diverge mid-generation or we hit an index OOB and fall back to the slow kernel. Reproduced intermittently on dedicated nodes with mixed fp16/quantized weights.

Symptoms observed (summary):
- Client request at seq_len ~ 4096 triggers an attention kernel selection path that later switches kernels mid-generation (fast->fallback).
- In some reproductions the model outputs garbled tokens starting at token ~ 4120. In others, the request aborts with an index OOB in KV cache read.
- Eviction logs show unexpected cache evictions during a single request (we expect no inter-request eviction).

Repro commands used (local + on-dedicated):
1) Repro with small harness:
   python -m repro.long_context_run --model rwi-ggml-7b --seq-len 4096 --batch 1 --quant q4f16 --device cuda:0 --trace kernels

2) Stress run across nodes (k8s job):
   ./infra/run_inference_stress.sh --image=redwood/serving:sha-20250212 --cmd "python -m server.run --config /etc/serve/longseq.yaml" --parallel 8 --duration 30m

3) Direct kernel trace (on node):
   NV_LOG_LEVEL=info NV_KERNEL_TRACE=1 ./bin/serve --model-dir /mnt/models/rwi-7b --enable-kv-cache --max-seq 8192 2>&1 | tee /tmp/kvtrace.log

Snippets from kvtrace.log (important bits):
[2026-02-18 16:12:03.762] kernel_selector: picked flash_attention_v2 (heuristic score 0.87) for seq_len=1024
[2026-02-18 16:12:03.764] kernel_selector: fallback to tiled_attention (score 0.45) after failed sanity check (mismatched strides)
[2026-02-18 16:12:03.766] kv_cache: read idx start=4090 len=64 kv_offset=262144 (OK)
[2026-02-18 16:12:03.767] kv_cache: attempted read idx start=4121 len=16 kv_offset=0 -> OOB: idx+len > cache_capacity (cap=4096)
[2026-02-18 16:12:03.770] runtime: aborting request, reason=kv-cache-oob

Hypotheses so far:
- Hypothesis A: Kernel selection heuristics compute expected strides/kv-shape using a sequence-length bucket that incorrectly assumes per-request seq_len rather than current generation length. This can cause a kernel mismatch mid-run when generation extends beyond initial seq_len assumption.
- Hypothesis B: KV cache indexing is using a global offset that doesn't get updated when the attention kernel switches (some kernels expect packed KV layout, others expect tiled layout) - mismatch leads to OOB reads.
- Hypothesis C: Eviction/compaction path triggers during long generation under memory pressure; eviction logic uses wall-clock time + token count heuristics and mistakenly considers the generating request as eligible for eviction (race).

Extra observations:
- When running with --disable-kernel-switching the reproducer does not fail (no OOB, no garbage tokens). This is strong evidence kernel-switching is a factor.
- The failure rate increases when mixed workloads are colocated on the same GPU (i.e., other pods doing batching). Suggests caching/allocations interference.
- On nodes with older CUDA (11.6) I see fewer instances; on nodes with 12.x it's more common (possible interaction with newer kernels / cutlass/flash-attention v2).

Commands tried to gather more info / quick fixes tried:
- Force single kernel path for long-seq via env var: RW_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=flash_attention_v2 (result: still saw stride mismatch warnings then fallback)
- Disable kernel switching at runtime flag: --force-kernel tiled_attention (result: stable, but ~2x slower)
- Increase kv_cache_capacity via config (kv_cache_capacity_tokens=16384) (result: reduced OOB frequency but didn't eliminate)
- Add extra barrier after kernel switch to re-compute offsets: PATCH local (see note below) (result: fairly effective locally but the patch is hacky)

Relevant code breadcrumbs (locations to inspect):
- kernel_selector/*: heuristics for stride/shape scoring and sanity checks (see pick_kernel_for_attention in kernel_selector.cpp)
- runtime/kv_cache.cpp: read/write offsets, eviction logic, per-request cache handle
- kernels/flash_attention_adapter.cu: layout adapter that maps our KV buffer into kernel-friendly layout
- serve/main.cpp: request lifetime and generation loop (where kernel-switch decisions happen)

Quick local patch (what I tried):
- After kernel selection changes, call kv_cache->recompute_layout(request_id) which recomputes per-kernel offsets and layout metadata. This avoids the OOB in my local reproducer.
- Patch location: runtime/serve/generation_manager.cpp:add recompute_layout() call when kernel != prev_kernel.
- Downsides: introduces an atomic barrier and small perf hit (~3-5% latency); needs broader correctness check (what about concurrent requests sharing memory pools?).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is cache layout per-request or global per-GPU? I need to re-audit comments in kv_cache.h. If global, then recompute on switch must be serialized globally.
- Why does kernel_selector fail the sanity check mid-generation? Are we re-using outdated metadata about model shape or kv_stride? Add logging around where shape metadata is captured.
- Can we make kernel selection deterministic for the duration of a request? If so, we might avoid mid-request switches entirely for long-running gens. Need to evaluate latency/cost impact.
- Add unit tests that simulate switching kernels in the same request (fake kernels that assert layout expectation).

Next concrete steps (near-term):
1) Add additional trace logging: log per-request kernel choice, per-token generation index, and kv-cache offsets at kernel boundaries (low overhead sampling).
2) Add a regression test to CI stress harness that forces kernel switch paths (emulate heuristic bounds).
3) Schedule a short spike to try serializing recompute_layout globally and run overnight stress on dedicated nodes.
4) Create a small PR that adds a fast-path to detect mismatch and abort cleanly with clearer metrics (instead of generic kv-cache-oob).

Notes to self (breadcrumbs for later):
- see PR #842 for my local recompute_layout attempt (draft); need to clean up tests and add comments re: concurrency.
- Filing JIRA-RT-1291 to track remediation and customer impact.

Unresolved / weird edgecases seen: 
- When switching from a quantized kernel to a FP16 kernel mid-generation the offsets are correct but values appear corrupted (possible mis-specified element-stride).
- Kernel adapter sometimes reports a stride of 0 in logs (this should never happen) - add an assert and capture trace.

If you pick this up: start by running the stress job with NV_KERNEL_TRACE=1 and reproduce once, then dump /tmp/kvtrace.log and grep for "kv-cache-oob" and "kernel_selector" entries. If you can't reproduce, try co-locating another batching job to increase interference.

-- Samira
